title: Isandro and the Static
premise: Sable Dravenmoor, a memory-clone grown from the corpse of the colony's murdered founder, has spent three years recording Meridian Station's slow decay while everyone above forgets it exists. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, Sable discovers the flicker was a signal: a dead man's message encoded in his own inherited memories, proof that the founder's murder and the war's origin are the same crime. Hunted by both fleets as the truce expires, Sable must carry the message to the neutral relay at the system's heart, choosing between exposing the truth that ends the war or destroying it to save the only home he has. He delivers it — and the war ends, but not before he learns he is not the first clone sent to die carrying it.
about_author: Ansel Galloway is a former orbital salvage archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the belongings of crews that never came home. He writes science fiction about the paperwork of apocalypse from a converted cargo module in the outer belt.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Sable records another day of Meridian's decay — failing recyclers, dwindling colonists — when gravity dies for exactly nine seconds and every loose object on the station hangs suspended. In the silence, he hears a voice in his own head: the original Dravenmoor's, saying coordinates he doesn't recognize. POV: Sable. Beat: dread disguised as routine, then rupture.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Sable digs into his own creation contract and finds a sealed attachment: the original was murdered mid-transmission of something called the Meridian Accord, and the clone was grown specifically to finish delivering it. The fleet liaison assigned to 'protect' him is clearly there to watch him. POV: Sable. Beat: the horror of learning your life has an agenda written into it.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Following the coordinates, Sable descends into the flooded lower decks where the original died, and his inherited memories begin triggering involuntarily — he relives fragments of the murder without consent. A dying engineer named Oyelaran confirms the original came here with a data core the night he was killed. POV: Sable. Beat: grief for a man whose death you remember firsthand.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Want a Word
chapters.summary: A Concord patrol and a Veyra boarding team arrive within hours of each other, both claiming jurisdiction over 'anomalous gravitational events.' Sable realizes the nine-second flicker wasn't an accident — someone detonated a memory-lattice weapon, and both sides think he's holding the trigger. POV: alternating Sable and Concord Captain Ives. Beat: paranoia tightening into a noose.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Ives reveals the ceasefire expires in eleven days; her superiors want Sable's inherited memories extracted by force before it does. Sable bargains for transport toward the neutral relay, hiding that he already knows what the message says — and that it implicates both fleets' founders equally. POV: Sable. Beat: the corrupting arithmetic of using people who are using you.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Lattice
chapters.summary: During transit, the original's memories surface fully: the founder discovered both fleets were seeded by the same corporation that built Meridian, and the war is its business model. Sable understands why clones were used as couriers — they're deniable, disposable, and their deaths erase the message. POV: Sable, deep in flashback. Beat: inheritance revealed as a trap dressed as a gift.

chapters.title: Oyelaran's Choice
chapters.summary: Veyra forces board the ship; Oyelaran sacrifices herself jamming their weapons, revealing she helped kill the original under orders and has been waiting years to undo it. She gives Sable the second half of the data core before the deck blows. POV: Oyelaran, then Sable. Beat: guilt finding its only available redemption, at full price.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Heart
chapters.summary: Sable reaches the neutral relay alone, pursued by both fleets, and begins transmission — but the relay demands verification from 'Dravenmoor, original,' forcing him to prove he counts as the man whose name he carries. Ives arrives with extraction orders and must choose between them and him. POV: Sable. Beat: identity as the final lock on the door.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ives stands down her guns and authenticates Sable as Dravenmoor; the Accord broadcasts system-wide, naming the corporation and the founding lie, and both fleets' rank-and-file refuse their launch orders as the truce expires. The war doesn't end with a treaty but with thousands of soldiers simply hearing the truth at once. POV: multiple, converging on Sable. Beat: climax — power broken not by force but by disclosure.

chapters.title: The Second Clone
chapters.summary: Weeks later, rebuilding Meridian, Sable receives a courier pod from the corporation's abandoned vaults: another clone of himself, grown years ago, sent to die on the same errand — still warm, still sleeping. Sable wakes him and begins recording a new archive: not a case file, but a warning about inheritance itself. POV: Sable. Beat: resolution — memory kept honestly, or not at all.
